Yes. The subtext enriches the story naturally rather than feeling forced. Miss Emily’s advice to call supermarket work “retail” conveys both class anxiety and protective concern, revealing the social rules Nora is learning to navigate. Her insistence that Nora have money of her own likewise expresses care through practical instruction rather than open affection.

The final adjustment of the coat’s cuffs brings this ambiguity together: the gesture can be both correction and tenderness. These moments deepen the characters’ relationship and make the story’s class-conscious social setting more vivid.
